_readme: Pilot data for the 'What it looks like' panel on questions.html. Hand-curated, not scraped: each image URL is hotlinked to its original publisher (never re-hosted) and was checked for reachability but not visually verified inside the build sandbox, which has no general internet access. Spot-check before wider use. Add countries incrementally -- the front end already shows a graceful 'no specimen found yet' note for every country with no entry here, so an empty entry set is a valid, honest starting state, not a bug. Round 5 (1 Sept 2026): UNHCR country help sites (Bolivia, Costa Rica, Ethiopia), RENAP Guatemala, Wikimedia Commons (Germany, Brazil), ONPAR Panama and NRC Kenya added; image URLs were confirmed to exist (HTTP-level) but not visually inspected, except Germany's Commons file which was opened in a browser.

USA.note: No document exists for this item in the US system — there is nothing to show here. Form I-94 and the Employment Authorization Document (EAD) are real US immigration documents, but the curated note above is explicit that they must NOT be introduced as a stand-in: neither is issued specifically for an asylum claim (I-94 is a general entry record, the EAD is issued for many immigration categories besides asylum), so showing either risks a false positive rather than helping a respondent recognise their situation.
